definition: A Vδ2 (TRDV2)-expressing mature gamma-delta T cell that additionally expresses CD161 (KLRB1) at the cell surface. CD161 is a C-type-lectin innate/memory-associated receptor shared across NK, alpha-beta, gamma-delta and MAIT lineages, so the distinguishing feature of this cell is the combination of CD161 with a Vδ2 gamma-delta TCR. Its natural parent is the Vdelta2-positive gamma-delta T cell. Despite occasional annotation as a MAIT cell, this is not a mucosal-associated invariant T cell: genuine MAIT cells are alpha-beta, TRAV1-2/MR1-restricted, whereas a TRDV2-positive cell carries a gamma-delta TCR.

logical_axioms.filler: killer cell lectin-like receptor subfamily B member 1
logical_axioms.notes: CD161 (KLRB1) surface expression, documented at the protein level by flow cytometry; a shared innate/memory marker, not gamma-delta-specific.
gamma-delta T cells of this subset exert perforin/granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity.

references.supports: Upstream tonsil single-cell study used as a starting annotation by the reference atlas.

Review establishing the definitional basis of the TRDV2 marker used in the atlas label. Human gamma-delta T cells are divided by TCR delta-chain (TRDV gene) usage into TRDV1+ (Vδ1+) and TRDV2+ (Vδ2+) subsets; TRDV2 is a transcript/gene-segment marker of the Vδ2 lineage. TRDV2+ (Vδ2+) cells dominate peripheral blood and pair almost exclusively TRGV9 with TRDV2 to form innate-like, phosphoantigen-reactive Vγ9Vδ2 T cells. This anchors TRDV2 as a gamma-delta (not alpha-beta) lineage marker.

Review defining CD161/KLRB1 as a marker and its expression on gamma-delta T cells. CD161 (KLRB1) is a C-type lectin membrane glycoprotein expressed on NK cells, ~24% of peripheral T cells, and on both alpha-beta and gamma-delta T cells; here CD161 is discussed as a surface/protein marker (flow/immunostaining) while KLRB1 is its gene. CD161 marks a memory phenotype in the gamma-delta compartment and is associated with tissue-homing (gut/liver) and shared with MAIT cells — the shared CD161 expression is a key source of the MAIT/γδ transcriptional overlap seen in the atlas label.

Functional study of human γδ T cell subsets that co-analyses TRDV2 and CD161. TRDV2+ (Vδ2) cells are the most prevalent circulating γδ subset and produce IFN-γ on activation. CD161 is examined here as a surface/protein memory-associated marker (measured by flow cytometry) on TRDV2+ γδ T cells alongside CD27/CD28, situating CD161 as a memory/pro-inflammatory marker on the Vδ2 subset. TRDV2 is a transcript-level marker; CD161 is protein/flow here.

Directly localises CD161+ T cells (including small numbers of TCRγδ+ cells and TCRVα7.2+ MAIT cells) within human tonsil by immunohistochemistry and multicolor flow cytometry. CD161+ cells were found predominantly in the interfollicular zone (IFZ) surrounding germinal centers. CD161 is measured here at the PROTEIN level (anti-CD161 mAbs, flow); the snippet explicitly distinguishes CD161+ TCRγδ+ T cells from CD161-high TCRVα7.2+ MAIT cells in tonsil — direct evidence anchoring both the tonsil localisation and the γδ-vs-MAIT distinction. NOTE: 'C' in this snippet is an OCR rendering of superscript '+'.

The foundational study of gamma-delta T cells specifically in human palatine tonsil (the atlas tissue). Flow cytometry showed ~1.56% of tonsillar T cells express the γδ TCR; immunohistology localised them preferentially to the crypt epithelium, less in surface epithelium, and fewest in the interfollicular space. γδ TCR is a protein/surface identification here. Establishes the palatine-tonsil location and rarity of the γδ T cell population that the atlas Vδ2+ label sits within.

Functional characterisation of Vδ2+ (TRDV2+) γδ T cells in human tonsil (and spleen) organoids. Vδ2+ γδ T cells increased in abundance in tonsil organoids in response to malaria parasites, in contrast to Vδ1+ cells which did not expand. Establishes γδ T cell effector functions (cytotoxic killing, pro-inflammatory cytokines, B cell help, antigen presentation) in a secondary lymphoid / tonsil context. Vδ2 identity is defined by TCR usage; functions are cytotoxic/effector.

Dissects which innate-like T cell lineages express CD161. Confirms gamma-delta T cells, iNKT cells, and MAIT cells can all express CD161 (protein/flow), and identifies MAIT cells separately by TCR-Vα7.2 staining — reinforcing that CD161 is shared across lineages and is NOT MAIT-specific. Supports the caveat that a CD161+ TRDV2+ cell is a γδ (Vδ2) cell with a shared CD161 marker, not a canonical MAIT cell.

Definitional MAIT-cell paper underpinning the γδ/MAIT caveat. Canonical MAIT cells are identified by MR1-5-OP-RU tetramer staining and use the TRAV1-2 (Vα7.2) alpha-beta TCR; CD161 (high) is a widely used surrogate MAIT marker but is imperfect and not specific. This establishes that genuine MAIT cells are alpha-beta / TRAV1-2 / MR1-restricted, so CD161 alone (or CD161 with a γδ TCR) does not define a MAIT cell.

Shows MR1-restricted, MAIT-like cells can occur outside the canonical TRAV1-2+ compartment and share high CD161/CD26 with MAIT cells, but formal MAIT identity is defined by MR1 restriction and the TRAV1-2 alpha-beta TCR. Provides the conceptual frame of 'MAIT-like' innate cells that share CD161 but differ in lineage — directly relevant to labelling a TRDV2+ γδ cell as 'MAIT-like' rather than MAIT.
Azimuth human_tonsil_v2 single-cell reference atlas (source of the cell-type annotation).

justification: CD161+ subset of the proposed Vdelta2-positive gamma-delta T cell (natural parent once that term exists); provisional parent CL:0000800. CD161=KLRB1 asserted with the generic (cross-species) PR class per CL convention. The atlas 'MAIT' label is a MAIT/γδ conflation — genuine MAIT are αβ/MR1-restricted.

## New term request: CD161-positive Vdelta2-positive gamma-delta T cell

**Proposed label:** CD161-positive Vdelta2-positive gamma-delta T cell

**Definition:** A Vδ2 (TRDV2)-expressing mature gamma-delta T cell that additionally expresses CD161 (KLRB1) at the cell surface. CD161 is a C-type-lectin innate/memory-associated receptor shared across NK, alpha-beta, gamma-delta and MAIT lineages, so the distinguishing feature of this cell is the combination of CD161 with a Vδ2 gamma-delta TCR. Its natural parent is the Vdelta2-positive gamma-delta T cell. Despite occasional annotation as a MAIT cell, this is not a mucosal-associated invariant T cell: genuine MAIT cells are alpha-beta, TRAV1-2/MR1-restricted, whereas a TRDV2-positive cell carries a gamma-delta TCR.

**Parent (is_a):** mature gamma-delta T cell (CL:0000800)

**Anatomical location:** lymphoid tissue (UBERON:0001744)

**Logical axioms:**
- `has plasma membrane part` (RO:0002104) some **killer cell lectin-like receptor subfamily B member 1** (PR:000025670) — CD161 (KLRB1) surface expression, documented at the protein level by flow cytometry; a shared innate/memory marker, not gamma-delta-specific.
- `capable of` (RO:0002215) some **T cell mediated cytotoxicity** (GO:0001913) — gamma-delta T cells of this subset exert perforin/granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity.

**Synonyms:**
- CD161-positive Vdelta2 gamma-delta T cell (exact)
- CD161-positive TRDV2-positive gamma-delta T cell (exact)
- KLRB1-positive Vδ2 T cell (related)

**References:**
- King et al. (2021). DOI: 10.1126/sciimmunol.abh3768 ; PMID:34623901 — Source single-cell atlas (Azimuth human_tonsil_v2).
- Shepherd et al. (2020). DOI: 10.3390/ijms21176144 ; PMID:32858901 — Review establishing the definitional basis of the TRDV2 marker used in the atlas label.
